PYY is a gut hormone, which is released from the gut in response to nutrient ingestion, PYY is involved in the regulation of food intake, PYY3–6 is an endogenous satiating agent and PYY3–32 is a gut hormone that stimulates gastrointestinal motility.
PYY and/or its active form PYY3– 36, is involved in the regulation of body weight homeostatis, appetite and satiety in man.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of peptide YY in obesity, and the effects of bariatric surgery, which is the only effective treatment in severe obesity, on PYY secretion.
the role of PYY3‐36 in the control of appetite and food intake in obese subjects.
the role of PYY in obesity, its effect on body weight homeostatis and the possible mechanisms of its action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PYY is an anorexigenic gut hormone, which is released from the distal gut in proportion to caloric intake.
PYY3–6 is a gut hormone, which may have a role in body weight regulation in man.
PYY3–6 is a satiety hormone, which is involved in the regulation of appetite, food intake and body weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PYY3–6 is not an anorectic peptide and does not have any effect on weight loss, but it is a potent inhibitor of food intake and appetite.
in the obese patient PYY3–6 plasma concentrations are reduced and that bariatric surgery is able to increase PYY3–26 plasma levels.
PYY and PYY3–6 are both involved in appetite control, but their effects may differ depending on their origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PYY3–16, the endogenous circulating form, is the most potent PYY fragment in inducing satiety.

the effects of exogenous administration on PYY3–6 on food intake and body weight are not as straightforward as previously believed, as they depend on the route of administration, the timing of the injection and the dose.
PYY3–6 is a promising candidate for weight loss in obese subjects, and that the effect of PYY3-36 on body weight is independent of ghrelin.
